comments.subject: Public Comments Form
comments.comment:
Please consider disallowing e-bikes/scooters/anything motorized on our lovely bike paths. I have witnessed 2 accidents in the last 3 months (one on Virgin River Trail and one on the Snow Canyon Parkway) where an e-biker ran into a pedestrian and another cyclist resulting in injuries for all parties.

Some of the new e-bikes are similar to mini-motorcycles. The speed is just too much for a winding, curvy path. Riding two abreast is not safe for a multi-use path, and even less so at a high rate of speed. If something has a motor, why is it allowed on the paths?

comments.subject: City Council-Note Item 6 "Consider approval of Resolution No. 2024-030R approving the City to be a co-signer of the State of Utah's Public Lands Amicus Brief."
comments.comment:
Dear St George City Council,

We are writing in response to last night's agenda item 6 ("Consider approval of Resolution No. 2024-030R approving the City to be a co-signer of the State of Utah's Public Lands Amicus Brief.") as residents of the City of Saint George and members of Conserve Southwest Utah.

Conserve Southwest Utah is strongly opposed to Utah's lawsuit challenging the federal government's control over federal public lands in the state. Washington County's water resources, wildlife habitats, scenic vistas, active communities, and tourism, recreation and real estate economies thrive because of federal public lands. Keeping local lands under federal protection is the best way to ensure long-term, enduring protections for the special places that mean so much to St. George residents.

Conserve Southwest Utah is a local nonprofit with supporters in the City of St. George whose mission is to conserve and steward our area's natural and cultural resources and advocate for Smart Growth policies that enable conservation for the benefit of present and future generations.

Thank you for your consideration of our comments on this issue.

Respectfully,

Judith Rognli, M.A.
City of St. George Resident
Desert Livability Program Manager, Conserve Southwest Utah

Susan Crook, ASLA, PLA
City of St. George Resident
Historical Landscape Architect
Member, Conserve Southwest Utah

notes: Two comments: Shawna Lacher (JotForm, e-bikes on bike paths) and Judith Rognli/Susan Crook (direct email on behalf of Conserve Southwest Utah re Resolution 2024-030R). Co-signed by Susan Crook.
